outcome: Nuclear apoptosis (apoptotic and non-apoptotic nuclei) in the lower uterine segment
cohort: The study included 28 controls and 82 women with one prior cesarean delivery, classified by time since their surgery (<=3 years, >3 and <=5 years, >5 and <=7 years, >7 and <=9 years, and >9 years).
finding: The lower uterine segment scar becomes stable at 3 years after cesarean delivery, and by 9 years, the scar is mature, with significant changes in smooth muscle and apoptosis observed over time.
mod_finding: The study found that the lower uterine segment scar following cesarean delivery shows significant changes in smooth muscle volume density and nuclear apoptosis over time, becoming stable at 3 years and mature by 9 years post-surgery.
cross-section timing: Women were examined at a single point in time, categorized based on the duration (ranging from <=3 years to >9 years) since their prior cesarean delivery.
